subject: Sequestered Dedicated pricing & KMS / audit log questions
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@acmehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-20T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial framing: single-tenant Dedicated + sequester premium

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I’m sending a concise framing for a Dedicated (single-tenant) deployment with the isolation/compliance items ACME asked about. Attached is a short SOW and a security appendix with KMS/audit-log options.

High-level pricing components:
- Baseline Dedicated commit: reserved GPU pool (4x A100-equivalent nodes) for 12 months at list rate.
- Single-tenant segmentation premium: +25% on top of baseline unit price to cover pool sequestering, network segmentation, and isolated control plane.
- Optional customer-managed KMS / HSM: one-time enablement + incremental $5k/mo for key management and integration (optional).
- Audit log retention: standard 90-day logs included; extended retention (1 year) +$2k/mo.
- Throughput guarantee: baseline throughput SLAs for token/sec; we can provide 99th percentile latency targets per route as part of the SOW.

Discounting / term levers:
- 12-mo commit: standard pricing above.
- 24-36-mo commit: potential to reduce segmentation premium to 15% and offer a usage discount tied to committed spend.

I’ve attached: SOW-draft.pdf and security-appendix.xlsx. If you want, I can map this to a single-line quote and a DocuSign ready SOW after we agree on term and premium.

Next step: would you prefer a 90-minute technical+procurement call next week to go line-by-line, or should I send a counter with numbers for a 36-month commit?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: SOW-draft.pdf (pdf), security-appendix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Elena Morales <elena@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, kim.lee@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-23T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial framing: single-tenant Dedicated + sequester premium

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear framing. A few quick clarifications from procurement and our security team:

1) The +25% segmentation premium is higher than we expected. Our target would be closer to a single-digit premium if we commit longer. Can you outline a counter that gets to ~10–15% for a 36-month commit?
2) For KMS: does +$5k/mo include HSM-backed keys and key rotation automation? We need FIPS/HSM for production PHI workloads.
3) Audit logs: we need 1 year retention and the ability to export logs to our SIEM (Splunk). Will that be supported and does that change pricing?
4) SLA/throughput: can you be explicit about what the 99th percentile latency guarantee covers (session length, prompt vs. completion)?

Procurement is pushing for a single price list (no surprises) and would prefer the isolation fee to be baked into an all-in number if possible.

If you can send a numeric counter with 36-mo committed spend, we’ll evaluate internally and share with legal/security.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Product, ACME Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-09-24T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: ACME questions — need pricing + security confirmation

Vanessa / Karthik —

FYI — ACME pushed back on the 25% segmentation premium and wants a 36-month committed counter with specifics on KMS/HSM and log export. Can we do the following:

- Prepare a numeric counter for 36 months (committed spend target: $1.2M ARR equivalent) with two options: (A) all-in price (segmentation baked in), (B) baseline + line items (segmentation, KMS, log retention).
- Confirm whether customer-managed KMS with HSM is feasible and confirm the one-time enablement vs recurring cost. Security needs to know FIPS/HSM level.
- Confirm throughput SLA wording and any credit formula.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-12345 — they’re at expansion stage, low legal friction but strict on PHI controls.

Thanks — Jordan
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-27T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: ACME questions — need pricing + security confirmation

Jordan / Karthik —

Proposed internal counter and constraints:

Pricing (36-month committed spend baseline $1.2M):
- Option 1 (All-in fixed): list-equivalent per-token price with segmentation premium baked in at +20% (all-in monthly invoice). We can offer a 10% committed usage discount on top of that for 36-mo to get effective unit reduction.
- Option 2 (Line-item): baseline pricing + segmentation premium at +18% + customer-managed KMS at $4k/mo recurring + one-time KMS enablement $4k. Extended log retention (1yr) +$2k/mo.

Notes on KMS/HSM:
- We support customer-managed keys with HSM (Cloud KMS / bring-your-own HSM). The $4k/mo number covers the operational overhead and auditability; one-time integration & key-handshake work is $4k (security-reviewed). This meets FIPS 140-2 validation for key storage depending on provider.

SLA / throughput:
- We will commit to route-level 99th percentile latency targets for prompt+completion up to a 2,000-token session; overages will be mitigated via batching policies.
- SLA credits: 10% of monthly invoice for a single month if 99th p breaches >3x in a 30-day window, escalating to higher credits with repeated events. Exact formula in SOW.

Compliance artifacts: we can share SOC 2 Type II summary, penetration test letters, and the security appendix. Legal should review.

I’ll attach a pricing-model.csv with the line items and monthly impact. If ACME wants a hard PO, Option 1 is simplest for procurement.

-Vanessa
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@acmehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, kim.lee@acmehealth.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-09-28T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Counter: 36-mo committed options (all-in vs line-item)

Elena —

Thanks for the clear asks. Per internal alignment, two tidy options are below. I’ve attached the SOW-draft, security appendix, and a pricing-model.csv that maps monthly impact. Also included a DocuSign stub if you want the all-in option executed quickly.

Option A — All-in (simplest for procurement)
- 36-month commit, baseline Reserved GPU pool (4x nodes): All-in monthly invoice with segmentation premium baked in.
- Effective segmentation premium: +20% on list, plus a 10% committed-usage discount across the term.
- Monthly invoice example (illustrative): $82,000/mo (all services, isolation, 90-day log retention) 
- KMS/HSM: included as optional add-on (see Option B).

Option B — Line-item (more transparent)
- Baseline monthly: $68,000
- Segmentation premium: +18% -> +$12,240/mo
- Customer-managed KMS (HSM): $4,000/mo recurring + $4,000 one-time enablement
- Extended 1yr log retention: +$2,000/mo
- Example total (with KMS + 1yr logs): $86,240/mo

SLA highlights: 99th percentile latency target for sessions <= 2,000 tokens; SLA credit formula included in SOW.

Next steps: tell me whether ACME prefers Option A or B and we’ll 1) update SOW with exact numbers, 2) generate DocuSign, 3) get security artifacts (SOC2 Type II summary + pentest letter) to your legal team.

Attachments: SOW-draft.pdf, security-appendix.xlsx, pricing-model.csv

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
DocuSign: https://docusign.com/EX-ACME-2026
From: Elena Morales <elena@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, kim.lee@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-04T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Counter: 36-mo committed options (all-in vs line-item)

Jordan —

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with our internal targets. Procurement prefers Option A (all-in) to simplify invoicing, provided legal can confirm the security appendix. Two quick asks before we issue a PO:

1) Please send SOC 2 Type II report summary and the most recent pentest letter to kim.lee@acmehealth.com.
2) Confirm that the KMS/HSM one-time enablement does not require additional network changes on our side beyond the key handshake and a short firewall rule (security team needs to verify).

If both check out, we’ll issue a PO for the 36-month all-in figure and sign the DocuSign SOW. Can we schedule a 30-min call next week for final sign-off?

Best,
Elena
Head of Product, ACME Health
---
